ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 2 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Fannie Lou Hamer

code.originalText: Two-week review of home blood pressure readings and the repeat urine test, with a kidney ultrasound and a nephrology telehealth consultation from the health center

text.paragraph: Two-week review of home blood pressure readings and the repeat urine test, with a kidney ultrasound and a nephrology telehealth consultation. [S]

Mrs. Hamer returns two weeks after her first visit. She took her home blood pressure twice a day for seven days with the cuff the health center gave her, and the community health worker helped her write the readings down; they average 152/94. Her thirst and frequent urination are already less on metformin, with some loose stools in the first week that have settled. She had her kidney ultrasound this morning at the health center, after the sonographer explained each step; she asked for her companion to stay in the room, and she did. She then spoke with Dr. Agbaje of nephrology by video from the clinic, with the community health worker beside her. Her SNAP and energy assistance applications have been sent. She asked why she needs two new medicines and what they will cost. [S]

list.item:
Hypertension with chronic kidney disease (I12.9). Home readings average 152/94 with clinic 156/96: stage 2 hypertension confirmed. ECG at intake showed sinus rhythm without left ventricular hypertrophy; TSH normal. With albumin in the urine, an ACE inhibitor is needed, and at this level two medicines are recommended from the start. [S]
Amlodipine 5 mg with benazepril 20 mg in one daily capsule, on the low-cost generic list.
Home readings twice a week.
Potassium and creatinine in one to two weeks at the health center.
Goal below 130/80.

Chronic kidney disease G2 A2 (N18.2). Repeat urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio 96 mg/g, confirming moderately increased albuminuria; eGFR 73. Ultrasound: right kidney 9.0 cm with a lower-pole cortical scar, left kidney 11.4 cm and normal, no blockage or stones. Dr. Agbaje judges the scarring consistent with her old injury, with diabetes and blood pressure adding to the albumin loss. [S]
Dapagliflozin 10 mg daily for kidney protection, at the discount pharmacy price; stop it on days she cannot eat or drink.
No ibuprofen or naproxen; acetaminophen for aching.
Urine albumin again in three to four months.

Type 2 diabetes (E11.65). Tolerating metformin extended-release 1,000 mg; symptoms easing. Dapagliflozin will also lower glucose without causing low blood sugar. [S]
Continue metformin.
Diabetes education class at the health center next month, with a ride arranged.

Food insecurity (Z59.41). SNAP application sent with the community health worker's help; health center food pantry and produce program started. [S]
Community health worker to follow the application.

Follow-up: Potassium and creatinine in one to two weeks at the health center, with a ride. Review in six weeks with lipids, retinal photographs and the second hepatitis B dose. Call for dizziness, ankle swelling, a cough that will not stop, swelling of the lips or tongue (call 911), or vomiting that stops her drinking. Next scheduled visit 2026-05-04: six-week review: blood pressure, kidney function and potassium after the new medicines, lipids, retinal photographs, and benefits. [S]
